sections.heading: Alcohol, drugs and occupant protection
sections.markdown:
## C — Alcohol, drugs and occupant protection

FACT_ID: sec04-F01 | anchor: A32
Driving while impaired by alcohol or another drug is unlawful. [A32]
Source: [A32 -> pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec04-F02 | anchor: A32
On Nebraska public roadways or public parking areas, neither a driver nor a passenger may consume alcohol or possess an open alcoholic-beverage container inside a vehicle. [A32]
Source: [A32 -> pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec04-F03 | anchor: A32
Alcohol and other drugs can impair safe vehicle control and sound driving decisions. [A32]
Source: [A32 -> pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec04-F04 | anchor: A32
Nebraska’s zero-tolerance alcohol rule applies to drivers younger than 21. [A32]
Source: [A32 -> pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec04-F05 | anchor: A32
Providing alcohol to a minor is unlawful and can create liability for resulting damage. [A32]
Source: [A32 -> pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec04-F06 | anchor: A32
For a driver younger than 21, a blood alcohol concentration of at least 0.02 percent makes driving unlawful. [A32]
Source: [A32 -> pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec04-F07 | anchor: A32
Driving with a blood alcohol concentration of at least 0.08 percent is unlawful regardless of age or vehicle type. [A32]
Source: [A32 -> pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec04-F08 | anchor: A32
Violating the alcohol-driving provisions can lead to criminal penalties or administrative license revocation. [A32]
Source: [A32 -> pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec04-F09 | anchor: A32
Driving on Nebraska roads constitutes agreement to chemical alcohol-or-drug testing when an officer requests it. [A32]
Source: [A32 -> pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec04-F10 | anchor: A32
Refusing an officer’s request for an alcohol-or-drug test of blood, breath or urine under Nebraska’s implied-consent rule is a separate crime. [A32]
Source: [A32 -> pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec04-F11 | anchor: A32
Failing, in the officer’s judgment, to complete a requested blood, breath or urine test for alcohol or drugs violates Nebraska’s implied-consent law. [A32]
Source: [A32 -> pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec04-F12 | anchor: A32
Refusing a requested alcohol-or-drug chemical test under Nebraska’s implied-consent law brings a one-year administrative license revocation. [A32]
Source: [A32 -> pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec04-F13 | anchor: A32
Criminal refusal penalties match the penalties for a DUI conviction involving blood alcohol concentration of at least 0.15 percent. [A32]
Source: [A32 -> pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec04-F14 | anchor: A32
Depending on prior convictions, a criminal refusal conviction may revoke the license for 2 through 15 years in addition to fines and jail. [A32]
Source: [A32 -> pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec04-F15 | anchor: A32
Significant impairment can appear well below the general unlawful alcohol concentration of 0.08 percent. [A32]
Source: [A32 -> pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec04-F16 | anchor: A32
Body weight is among the factors affecting alcohol absorption. [A32]
Source: [A32 -> pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec04-F17 | anchor: A32
Body composition associated with sex is among the factors affecting alcohol absorption. [A32]
Source: [A32 -> pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec04-F18 | anchor: A32
Food in the digestive tract is among the factors affecting alcohol absorption. [A32]
Source: [A32 -> pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec04-F19 | anchor: A32
The amount of time spent drinking is among the factors affecting alcohol absorption. [A32]
Source: [A32 -> pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec04-F20 | anchor: A32
A drinker who seems in control may still have seriously impaired driving ability. [A32]
Source: [A32 -> pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec04-F21 | anchor: A32
Simple reaction time is impaired at a blood alcohol concentration of 0.04 percent. [A32]
Source: [A32 -> pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec04-F22 | anchor: A32
Choosing between possible responses becomes impaired beginning at a blood alcohol concentration of 0.03 percent. [A32]
Source: [A32 -> pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec04-F23 | anchor: A33
Tracking a single object becomes impaired at a blood alcohol concentration of 0.05 percent. [A33]
Source: [A33 -> pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec04-F24 | anchor: A33
Tracking several objects can be impaired at an alcohol concentration lower than that needed to impair tracking one object. [A33]
Source: [A33 -> pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec04-F25 | anchor: A33
Dividing attention across tasks can be impaired below a blood alcohol concentration of 0.05 percent. [A33]
Source: [A33 -> pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec04-F26 | anchor: A33
At a blood alcohol concentration of 0.05 percent, understanding what was seen or heard takes longer. [A33]
Source: [A33 -> pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec04-F27 | anchor: A33
At a blood alcohol concentration of 0.05 percent, eye-movement control and combining visual images decline. [A33]
Source: [A33 -> pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec04-F28 | anchor: A33
Seeing detail in a moving object declines at a blood alcohol concentration of 0.05 percent. [A33]
Source: [A33 -> pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec04-F29 | anchor: A33
Hand-and-foot coordination and other precise muscular tasks are impaired at a blood alcohol concentration of 0.05 percent. [A33]
Source: [A33 -> pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec04-F30 | anchor: A33
A blood alcohol concentration of 0.08 percent impairs steering, braking, speed control, lane tracking, gear changes and distance judgments. [A33]
Source: [A33 -> pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec04-F31 | anchor: A33
Emergency response is impaired at a blood alcohol concentration of 0.04 percent. [A33]
Source: [A33 -> pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec04-F32 | anchor: A33
If drinking is planned, arrange a designated driver or another form of transportation. [A33]
Source: [A33 -> pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec04-F33 | anchor: A33
Only elapsed time reduces the body’s alcohol level and its effects. [A33]
Source: [A33 -> pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec04-F34 | anchor: A33
The handbook contrasts concentration on one task at a BAC as high as 0.08 percent with impaired divided attention below 0.05 percent. [A33]
Source: [A33 -> pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec04-F35 | anchor: A34
A child-restraint violation carries a twenty-five-dollar fine plus court costs and one point on the operator’s record. [A34]
Source: [A34 -> pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec04-F36 | anchor: A34
A general occupant-protection violation carries a twenty-five-dollar fine plus court costs. [A34]
Source: [A34 -> pdf-0034]

Misconceptions: Airbags supplement belts, and impairment can begin below the general unlawful alcohol threshold.
Mnemonics: Belt first, airbag added; sober driving needs sober decisions.
Glossary: BAC means blood alcohol concentration; implied consent describes agreement to chemical testing by driving; a primary law can support a stop by itself.
Dynamic facts: Changing contacts, officials, live services and fees are withheld from the stable rule inventory.

sections.heading: Alcohol, drugs and occupant protection
sections.markdown:
## C2 — Alcohol, drugs and occupant protection

FACT_ID: sec04-R01 | anchor: A33
A primary-law violation alone allows an officer to stop and ticket a driver. [A33]
Source: [A33 -> pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec04-R02 | anchor: A33
A secondary-law citation requires the driver to have been stopped and ticketed for another violation. [A33]
Source: [A33 -> pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec04-R03 | anchor: A33
Airbags add protection but do not replace seat-belt use. [A33]
Source: [A33 -> pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec04-R04 | anchor: A33
Combining seat belts with airbags improves crash protection. [A33]
Source: [A33 -> pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec04-R05 | anchor: A33
In a vehicle with a steering-wheel airbag, the recommended hand positions are nine o’clock and three o’clock. [A33]
Source: [A33 -> pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec04-R06 | anchor: A33
An airbag deployment can injure children, older occupants or short adults even in a low-speed crash. [A33]
Source: [A33 -> pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec04-R07 | anchor: A33
For greatest safety, children aged 12 or younger should ride in a rear seat. [A33]
Source: [A33 -> pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec04-R08 | anchor: A33
Never put a rear-facing infant seat in the front passenger position of an airbag-equipped vehicle. [A33]
Source: [A33 -> pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec04-R09 | anchor: A34
A driver in an airbag-equipped vehicle should leave at least 10 inches between the body and steering wheel. [A34]
Source: [A34 -> pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec04-R10 | anchor: A34
A child must ride rear-facing up to age 2 or until the child reaches the seat manufacturer’s upper height or weight limit. [A34]
Source: [A34 -> pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec04-R11 | anchor: A34
Children younger than 8 must be properly secured in a federally approved child safety seat. [A34]
Source: [A34 -> pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec04-R12 | anchor: A34
A child younger than 8 must occupy an available nonfront seat equipped with a restraint system when that seat is not already occupied by another child younger than 8. [A34]
Source: [A34 -> pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec04-R13 | anchor: A34
The child-seat and available-nonfront-seat requirements for children younger than 8 are primary laws. [A34]
Source: [A34 -> pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec04-R14 | anchor: A34
Children from age 8 until age 18 must use a seat belt or child safety seat. [A34]
Source: [A34 -> pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec04-R15 | anchor: A34
The restraint requirement for children aged 8 through 17 is a secondary law. [A34]
Source: [A34 -> pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec04-R16 | anchor: A34
Children younger than 18 may not ride in vehicle cargo areas. [A34]
Source: [A34 -> pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec04-R17 | anchor: A34
The prohibition on children riding in cargo areas is a primary law. [A34]
Source: [A34 -> pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec04-R18 | anchor: A34
All passengers must be buckled when the driver holds a provisional operator permit or a school permit. [A34]
Source: [A34 -> pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec04-R19 | anchor: A34
The passenger-restraint rule for provisional or school permit drivers is a secondary law. [A34]
Source: [A34 -> pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec04-R20 | anchor: A34
Child-restraint requirements apply throughout the vehicle’s seating positions. [A34]
Source: [A34 -> pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec04-R21 | anchor: A34
Childcare providers must secure every child in an appropriate safety seat or seat belt. [A34]
Source: [A34 -> pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec04-R22 | anchor: A34
A childcare provider’s failure to secure children can result in revocation of the childcare license. [A34]
Source: [A34 -> pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec04-R23 | anchor: A34
The child-restraint requirement for childcare providers is a primary law. [A34]
Source: [A34 -> pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec04-R24 | anchor: A34
Drivers and front-seat passengers must wear a seat belt or use a child safety seat. [A34]
Source: [A34 -> pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec04-R25 | anchor: A34
The front-seat occupant-protection requirement also applies in autocycles. [A34]
Source: [A34 -> pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec04-R26 | anchor: A34
The general driver-and-front-passenger belt requirement is a secondary law. [A34]
Source: [A34 -> pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec04-R27 | anchor: A34
Never leave a child alone or unsupervised in a vehicle. [A34]
Source: [A34 -> pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec04-R28 | anchor: A34
A pet left in a vehicle can suffer fatal heatstroke in minutes even when outdoor temperatures seem mild. [A34]
Source: [A34 -> pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec04-R29 | anchor: A34
Do not leave pets inside a motor vehicle. [A34]
Source: [A34 -> pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec04-R30 | anchor: A34
In a passenger vehicle, swerving to avoid a deer increases the risk of death or injury. [A34]
Source: [A34 -> pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec04-R31 | anchor: A34
When a deer impact is imminent, brake firmly, keep steering control and stop as safely as possible. [A34]
Source: [A34 -> pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec04-R32 | anchor: A34
Do not veer off the road, lose control or enter oncoming traffic to avoid a deer. [A34]
Source: [A34 -> pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec04-R33 | anchor: A34
Reduce deer-crash risk by improving your view, slowing in deer-warning zones and keeping speed within headlight range. [A34]
Source: [A34 -> pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec04-R34 | anchor: A34
Be alert for deer during dusk-to-dawn periods, in spring or fall, and near water or wooded areas. [A34]
Source: [A34 -> pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec04-R35 | anchor: A34
After seeing a deer, look for additional deer because they travel in groups and behave unpredictably. [A34]
Source: [A34 -> pdf-0034]
